newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn sees EU GAN sale pressure - source.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn sees EU GAN sale pressure - source.

text.p: France Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn, who spoke to the National Assembly's finance committee on Wednesday, believes the European Commission will require privatisation of state-owned insurer GAN, a parliamentary source said.

The previous centre-right government had applied to the Commission in Brussels for approval of a 20-billion-franc aid plan for GAN and had promised that the company would be sold off to the private sector, but the situation has been unclear since the left ousted the centre-right in a June 1 election.
Strauss-Kahn told members of the committee "GAN's financing needs will be 10 billion francs more than forecast," according to the source.

It was not clear whether Strauss-Kahn meant 10 billion more than the amount GAN was already due to receive this year in a capital injection as part of the previous government's total 20-billion-franc bailout plan.
"In the current climate, he judged the European partners would impose privatisation," said the source.
The Commission, which has to approve state aid to companies in the European Union, had already urged privatisation when it approved a previous much smaller aid package to GAN.
